title: VC 5 cassava: Characteristics
metaDescription: VC 5 cassava is an industrial cassava variety from ViSCA (now VSU). See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: VC 5 cassava is an industrial cassava variety. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from ViSCA (now VSU).

heroImage.alt: Kamote vines on long raised ridges in San Rafael, Bulacan, the kind of farm where VC 5 cassava is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cassava variety finder](/crop-varieties/cassava), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** High HCN (bitter), starch millers prefer high cyanide types.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the starch mills' variety: over 3,000 ha in Lanao in the 1990s, planted for its high yield. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant VC 5 cassava

Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of VC 5?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
